title: OpenAI Quietly Lists a New Life Sciences Model, Targeting the Drug-Tool Supplier Track
source_used: TestingCatalog original (fetched by this agent; published 10 Oct 2026 14:57 UTC) and BigGo Finance's rewrite with analysis (fulltext fetched by main session)
key_facts: OpenAI's API pricing page lists a new, officially unannounced model, gpt-rosalind-discovery, under 'Life sciences models' beside gpt-rosalind-research; the listing was first shared by the AI Tracker Bot on X and TestingCatalog reported it on 10 Oct 2026.
Both models are priced the same: $5 per million input tokens, $0.50 per million cached input tokens and $25 per million output tokens.
There is no blog post, help article or system card for the new model; BigGo says third-party checks found the Rosalind documentation pages return 404 errors.
The pricing page says billing for gpt-rosalind-research began on 5 Oct 2026, with access restricted to approved internal research through OpenAI's trusted-access program.
TestingCatalog says the name suggests a drug-discovery model but that this is a guess.
GPT-Rosalind launched in April 2026 for biology, drug discovery and translational medicine, with Amgen, Moderna, the Allen Institute and Thermo Fisher Scientific among early partners.
BigGo adds its own analysis: OpenAI acts as a tool supplier to drug companies rather than doing drug research itself, and the field still lacks large-scale clinical validation.
quote_evidence: OpenAI's API pricing page seems to have been updated to include a new model the company hasn't officially announced yet.
There's still no blog post, help article, or system card for it yet.
For now, though, that's a guess.
why_it_matters_hint: OpenAI appears to be building a family of life-sciences models, but nothing is known about what the new one does.
notes: Same TestingCatalog story our 11 Oct 2026 edition carried as item 57 (same link).
